decisions.executionNote: Approach the right-side red nut with an open gripper, gradually pitching downward while preserving elbow-up continuity; final alignment will use wrist RGB.
Finish vertical approach orientation and translate toward the red nut, keeping clearance and checking wrist centering before descending.
Lower and refine right red-nut alignment while the left arm begins a separate elbow-up approach to the yellow nut; both grippers remain open.
Center and close on the red nut, then make a small retention-test lift. Continue the left open-gripper approach to the yellow nut without crossing workspaces.
Lift the visibly retained red nut and carry it toward the red screw. Descend onto and close around the yellow nut with the left hand, then test retention with a short lift.
Bring the red nut above its matching screw and lower conservatively for alignment. Lift the retained yellow nut and start moving it toward a central staging area.
Corrected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Seat the red nut and begin clockwise tightening. Carry yellow toward center while remaining left of the right arm.
Continue red tightening, then open and reset the wrist without undoing the nut. Move held yellow to the central staging point, keeping arm separation.
Regrasp and tighten red through another clockwise stroke. Set yellow upright at center, open the left gripper, then lift slightly to clear it.
Red appears seated with the bolt tip nearly flush; release and clear it, then approach the purple nut. Withdraw the left arm from the staged yellow nut, maintaining separation.
Approach the purple nut from above and restore a vertical grasp orientation. Red remains upright after release; left stays clear while the right aligns.
Use the wrist image to correct the purple nut's lateral offset and descend toward grasp height, leaving a small clearance for another visual check.
Close around the centered purple nut and lift to verify retention. Move the left hand farther aside before staging the purple nut for a handover.
Purple is visibly retained. Lift clear of the completed red pair and carry purple toward a separate central staging spot in front of yellow; left remains clear.
Move purple to the center-front staging point and lower it upright toward the table, staying on the right side of the midline.
Release purple upright at center-front, lift clear, then separate the hands laterally before the left approaches purple and the right approaches staged yellow.
Approach the two separately staged nuts: left to purple at center-front and right to yellow behind it. Maintain front-back clearance and stop above grasp height for RGB alignment.
Correct the small lateral offsets and descend vertically onto both staged nuts, preserving their front-back separation and keeping both grippers open until alignment is checked.
Grasp both staged nuts, lift vertically to verify retention, then separate left with purple and right with yellow toward their own workspaces.
Both nuts are visibly retained. Raise for bolt clearance and transport purple left and yellow right above their matching screws, avoiding the assembled red pair.
Lower both retained nuts over their matching screw axes. Correct yellow slightly right using wrist RGB and slow the final descent to check seating before tightening.
Seat purple and yellow gently, then apply matching clockwise tightening strokes while keeping both grippers closed. Check bolt-tip depth and alignment afterward.
Wrist RGB shows the purple bolt beside rather than inside its nut; yellow alignment is also uncertain. Lift both retained nuts and restore a common viewing orientation before correcting their axes.
Correct the small lateral offsets and level both nut axes, then lower slowly without turning so the next wrist view can confirm whether each bolt is centered in its hole.
Both bolt tips now appear within the nut openings. Remove residual tilt while preserving fingertip alignment, seat gently, and test a short clockwise turn before a longer tightening stroke.

The short turn exposed residual off-axis seating. Lift clear, restore the shared viewing orientation, and move each nut slightly toward the robot to center over its bolt before another slow insertion.
Both bolt tips are visible inside the openings after the correction. Refine lateral centering, lower slowly to engage, then make a moderate clockwise tightening stroke with both hands closed.
Refine the remaining millimeter-scale axis offset, then continue clockwise tightening with a small downward feed; both bolt tips remain visible within the nut openings.
Open both grippers and reset wrist yaw for another tightening stroke without reversing the nuts; inspect whether the nuts stay supported and aligned on their bolts.
Both nuts fell free on release, so they were not threaded. Reapproach the visible nuts beside their bolts for fresh, centered grasps; leave the red assembly untouched.
The right open fingers are contacting the nearby yellow bolt. Lift and yaw both grippers for clearance before descending again toward the loose nuts.
Use the rotated wrist views to center each loose nut, descend to grasp height, close, and lift clear for a fresh retention check.
Both nuts are retained again. Lift above the bolts, restore a common vertical wrist view, and translate toward the matching bolt axes for a fresh alignment check.
Lower without turning to observe insertion directly. Correct yellow left and toward the robot; purple is nearly laterally centered but has a different grasp offset, so its descent remains vertical.
Both bolt tips are centered in the openings. Apply a slow clockwise stroke with gradual downward feed to engage the threads, keeping each nut firmly held.
Finish the clockwise stroke, release both nuts, and reset wrist yaw. Check whether each remains supported on its matching bolt before another tightening cycle.
Purple remains supported on its bolt after release, so regrasp and tighten further. Yellow came free; lift the right hand and reposition above its resting area for recovery.
Reset the open left wrist for another purple tightening stroke. Approach the loose yellow nut with the right gripper yawed away from the adjacent bolt, stopping above pickup height for alignment.
Regrasp purple slightly lower and continue clockwise tightening. Finish aligning and grasping yellow with the fingers rotated clear of its bolt, then lift for visual verification.
Release and reset the purple tightening grip without reversing the nut. Yellow is retained; lift it over the bolt, restore a front-facing wrist view, and translate toward the bolt axis.
Regrasp purple lower on the nut and add another clockwise tightening stroke. Lower yellow vertically over its bolt with a small centering correction, pausing before rotation to inspect engagement.
Release purple and lift clear to inspect its final seating. Yellow's bolt is centered in the opening; seat slightly deeper and apply a controlled clockwise tightening stroke.
Purple remains upright on its matching bolt after release. Withdraw the left arm toward home while resetting the open right wrist, checking whether yellow now stays engaged.
Yellow now stays supported after release. Regrasp it slightly lower and add a clockwise tightening stroke while returning the left arm toward its origin with gradual pitch recovery.
Finish returning the left arm to origin. Open the right gripper and reset its yaw while leaving yellow supported, preparing another tightening stroke.
Yellow stays on its bolt with the gripper open. Adjust grip height slightly, regrasp, and apply another clockwise tightening stroke with a small downward feed; left remains at origin.
Reset the right wrist with the gripper open, then regrasp yellow slightly lower for another tightening stroke. The other two pairs remain undisturbed.
Apply a longer clockwise stroke to yellow with a gradual downward feed, maintaining the closed grip and leaving the left arm at origin.
Release yellow after the tightening stroke, lift the open gripper clear, and reset yaw. Inspect that all three matched pairs remain upright before returning the right arm home.
All three matched pairs remain upright after release. Return the open right arm toward origin with gradual pitch recovery and elbow-up continuity; keep the left arm home.
Complete the right arm's final small return to origin and hold both grippers open, leaving all three assembled pairs undisturbed.
The episode remains active; upright placement alone does not establish full thread depth. Reapproach purple and red for close inspection and additional tightening if needed, leaving yellow untouched.
The close view shows red's bolt nearly flush and purple seated on its bolt. Avoid disturbing the assembled pairs; withdraw both open hands along the continuous approach path back toward origin.
Make the final millimeter-scale home corrections, then hold both arms at origin with grippers open while the three matched assemblies remain undisturbed.
Hold both open grippers at origin and let the assemblies settle. All three pairs remain upright in RGB; exact thread depth is not directly measurable from this view.
Revisit only purple for a closer depth check and, if needed, a final tightening stroke. Keep the right arm home and preserve clearance above the assembled pair.
The close purple view shows the bolt tip nearly flush in the nut, so avoid further disturbance. Retract the open left arm along its continuous approach path; right remains at origin.
Correct the final small home-position residuals, then hold both arms at origin with grippers open. Leave the three upright matched assemblies undisturbed.
Maintain both open grippers at origin. The matched assemblies remain upright and stable; avoid disturbing their seating while the episode remains active.
Hold both arms at origin with grippers open, preserving the three stable matched assemblies without further contact.
Reapproach red alone to check and finish its tightening depth; its earlier tightening was shorter than the others. Keep the left arm home and maintain clearance above the assembly.
Red's bolt is visibly flush, so leave it untouched. Move the open right hand above yellow for a clear depth inspection while maintaining clearance from both assembled pairs.
Yellow still shows several exposed internal threads above its bolt tip. Regrasp the supported nut for additional clockwise tightening without lifting it from the bolt.
Apply a controlled two-radian clockwise tightening stroke to yellow with a small downward feed, keeping the supported nut grasped and the left arm at home.
Release yellow without lifting it and reset wrist yaw for another tightening stroke. Inspect its thread depth and support before regrasping; left remains home.
Yellow remains supported after release. Regrasp and add another clockwise stroke with a slow downward feed to reduce the remaining exposed thread depth.
Release and reset the right wrist without lifting yellow. Recheck the nut's support and remaining axis offset before further tightening; keep the other pairs undisturbed.
Raise the open right hand slightly to grip only the upper nut, avoiding possible contact with the bolt shaft. Regrasp and test a shorter clockwise turn; leave the other pairs untouched.
Finish the upper-nut tightening stroke slowly, then release without lifting or reversing it. Check that yellow remains supported and centered.
Yellow remains supported with fewer exposed threads. Reset the open wrist, correct the small grip-center offset, and regrasp the upper nut for another controlled tightening stroke.
Remove the small wrist tilt while preserving the nut center, then tighten yellow clockwise through another two radians with a slow downward feed.
Open and reset the right wrist, raising it only four millimeters to isolate the upper nut from the bolt shaft before the next grip. Yellow remains supported; the other pairs stay untouched.
Regrasp the upper yellow nut and apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with two millimeters of downward feed. Keep the other assembled pairs undisturbed.
Release yellow and lift the open hand clear before returning home. Its bolt tip appears near the nut opening; inspect that the assembly remains supported without further contact.
Yellow remains upright after release, with its bolt tip near flush. Return the open right arm to origin using gradual translation and pitch recovery; leave all assemblies undisturbed.
The final home step was rejected by the continuity guard. Replan from the observed pose with much smaller increments, then hold both arms at origin with open grippers.
Maintain both arms at origin with grippers open. All three matched assemblies remain upright and stable after release; avoid further disturbance while the episode remains active.
